statusText: Green - every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue, while better-verified reporting shows the Riyadh attack did reach an Aramco-branded fuel tank at an airport depot without touching production or export capacity
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because every published hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Verified reporting firms the Riyadh picture - an Aramco-branded fuel tank burned at an airport depot and was extinguished - while Hormuz throughput runs at a six-month high and equity futures stay halted until 22:00Z Sunday
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the final observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, which is the last slot published in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September; the 10-year had touched 5.04% earlier in the week, its highest since 2007. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%, as concern over the Saudi East-West pipeline disruption eased. The material change since the previous published hour is a correction to the damage picture rather than a new event. Earlier hours relied on the coalition statement that the Riyadh missile was intercepted with no damage; AFP-sourced reporting carried by France 24 and corroborated by The Times of Israel establishes that a fuel tank bearing the Aramco logo burned at a depot near King Khalid International Airport and was extinguished by firefighters, and that FlightRadar24 briefly listed the airport at its maximum disruption index of 5.0 before traffic resumed. No casualties have been reported. That is a real infrastructure impact, but at the fuel-distribution end rather than production or export capacity, and no reporting indicates a production outage. The counterweight is unchanged and specific: CENTCOM's Admiral Brad Cooper said Saturday that Hormuz oil and LNG transits reached a six-month high over the past two weeks, with more than a billion barrels moved in recent months against roughly ten million barrels a day of transit. The shared cross-asset context collected at 21:48Z is 107 minutes old at this assessment, past its 90-minute freshness limit, and was already partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; it is therefore treated as stale and is not carried into the scoring here, which rests on independently verified primary-source marks. Two scheduled items sit just beyond this window and shape the Stress path into the restart. Nasdaq has confirmed SpaceX's index weight at 2.82%, up from roughly 1.28%, with the rebalance taking effect Monday across tracking assets reported above $800 billion including the $482 billion QQQ. A Trump-Xi summit is widely reported for Washington on 24 September, but the time remains unscheduled and confirmation has not been uniform, so it is omitted from the verified event calendar and named only as a week-ahead checkpoint. Tail is held at 4, the floor of a closed venue, because no hour in this window offers a mechanism for mean reversion to fail. Stress 24 carries the weekend's headline accumulation toward a single reopening auction, which this window now contains in its final hour. Confidence rises to 74 because the damage ambiguity that limited the previous hours is resolved across three independent outlets and every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources, offset by a stale shared context and another hour of distance from the tape.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail entered the window at 6, eased to 5 and held there for twenty-two consecutive slots before stepping to 4 in the final hour. Stress decayed from 27 through 21, held 21 for five hours, then drifted back through 22, 23 and 24 into the closing slots. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence fell steadily from 85 to 72 before recovering one point to 73 once Saudi authorities confirmed the Riyadh interception, with the unverified strike file named repeatedly as the limiting factor.
outlookSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt and the final slot contains the restart: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 10:00Z, 7 from 13:00Z, 8 from 16:00Z, 9 from 19:00Z and 10 from 21:00Z, reaching 11 in the restart hour - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the halt is Saudi Arabia's Tadawul session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z, the first market-based read on the Riyadh depot fire and the Yanbu claims. Monday's confirmed Nasdaq-100 rebalance, which lifts SpaceX to a 2.82% weight, falls after every hour published here but is named as a checkpoint because pre-positioning can reach the restart. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified.

drivers: About 24h since the Riyadh air-raid alert sounded shortly before 03:00 local time
